ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AE$ and $AD$ are respectively the altitude and the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$, and $\angle B=40^\circ$, $\angle C=60^\circ$, find the degree measure of $\angle DAE$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle B = 40^\circ$ and $\angle C = 60^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle BAC = 180^\circ - \angle B - \angle C = 80^\circ$.\\
Since $AD$ is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$, \\
it follows that $\angle BAD = \angle DAC = \frac{1}{2} \angle BAC = 40^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle ADE = \angle B + \angle BAD = 80^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle DAE = 90^\circ - \angle ADE = 90^\circ - 80^\circ = \boxed{10^\circ}$.
